chapters.1.summary: King Ahasuerus rules one hundred twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia. In his third year he displays his wealth for six months. He then gives a seven-day feast in the palace garden. Queen Vashti holds a feast for the women. On the seventh day the king, merry with wine, sends for her. She refuses to come. His advisers fear that all wives will now despise their husbands. A royal law removes Vashti and orders every man to rule his house.
chapters.1.lds: The Seminary lesson starts with the decision to replace Vashti. How do the advisers turn one refusal into rules for wives?
chapters.2.summary: The king’s servants propose gathering beautiful young women for him to choose from. Mordecai, a Jew of Benjamin, lives in Susa. He has raised his orphaned cousin Esther as a daughter. Esther is taken to the palace and wins the keeper’s favor. She does not reveal her people, as Mordecai told her. After a year of preparation she goes to the king. He loves her more than the others and makes her queen. Mordecai uncovers a plot to kill the king, and it is written in the records.
chapters.2.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Mordecai’s care for Esther. How does he help her after she becomes queen?
chapters.3.summary: The king promotes Haman the Agagite above all the officials. Everyone at the gate bows to him except Mordecai. Haman learns Mordecai is a Jew and decides to destroy all Jews. He casts lots to choose a day. He tells the king that a certain people ignores the king’s laws. He offers a huge sum, and the king gives him his ring. Letters go to every province to kill all Jews on one day. The king and Haman sit down to drink, and Susa is confused.
chapters.3.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Haman’s anger. How does his anger at Mordecai threaten all the Jews?
chapters.4.summary: Mordecai tears his clothes and wails in sackcloth at the king’s gate. Jews in every province fast and weep. Esther sends a servant to learn what has happened. Mordecai sends a copy of the decree and asks her to plead with the king. She answers that anyone who approaches unsummoned may die. Mordecai replies that she will not escape in the palace. Esther asks all the Jews of Susa to fast three days. She will go to the king: “If I perish, I perish.”
chapters.4.lds: Come, Follow Me studies courage and fasting. What help does Esther ask for before approaching the king?
chapters.5.summary: On the third day Esther puts on royal robes and stands in the inner court. The king holds out his golden scepter and offers her up to half the kingdom. She invites him and Haman to a banquet. At the banquet she invites them to a second one tomorrow. Haman leaves happy until he sees Mordecai, who will not rise. At home he boasts of his riches, sons, and honors. He says none of it satisfies him while Mordecai sits at the gate. His wife suggests a gallows fifty cubits high.
chapters.5.lds: Come, Follow Me compares Esther’s risk with Haman’s pride. Why do his honors fail to satisfy him?
chapters.6.summary: That night the king cannot sleep and has the royal records read to him. He hears how Mordecai exposed the plot against him. He learns that Mordecai received nothing. Haman arrives to ask for Mordecai’s death. The king asks how to honor a man the king favors. Haman thinks this means himself and describes a royal robe and horse. The king tells him to do all this for Mordecai. Haman leads Mordecai through the city and goes home in mourning.
chapters.6.lds: The Seminary lesson recalls the king’s records. How does the saved report change Mordecai’s treatment?
chapters.7.summary: The king and Haman come to Esther’s second banquet. The king again asks what she wants. She asks for her life and the life of her people. They have been sold to be destroyed. The king asks who has dared to do this. Esther answers, “An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!” The king storms out and returns to find Haman fallen on Esther’s couch. Haman is hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai.
chapters.7.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Haman’s choices and their results. How does Esther explain the danger to the king?
chapters.8.summary: The king gives Haman’s estate to Esther and his ring to Mordecai. Esther falls at the king’s feet and weeps. She begs him to cancel Haman’s letters. The king says a sealed decree cannot be reversed. He lets them write a new one in his name. It allows the Jews in every city to gather and defend their lives. Couriers ride out on royal horses. Mordecai leaves in royal robes, and Susa rejoices.
chapters.8.lds: Come, Follow Me studies fasting during danger. Why must Esther keep asking for help after Haman dies?
chapters.9.summary: On the thirteenth day of Adar the Jews gather and strike those who attack them. Officials help them out of fear of Mordecai. In Susa they kill five hundred men and Haman’s ten sons. Esther asks for a second day in Susa. Across the provinces seventy-five thousand enemies die. The Jews take no plunder. They rest and feast on the next day. Mordecai and Esther write letters that make the feast of Purim yearly.
chapters.9.lds: Come, Follow Me connects Esther’s courage with later joy. How do gifts help people remember the rescue?
chapters.10.summary: King Ahasuerus lays a tax on the land and the coasts. His acts of power are written in the royal records. The records also tell of the greatness of Mordecai. Mordecai the Jew is second to the king. He is great among the Jews and well liked by his many kin. He seeks the good of his people. He speaks peace to all their children.
chapters.10.lds: Mordecai works for his people’s good. Who benefits from the power he receives?
